correctness.rationale:
In the full stated domain, each vertex has exactly \(2r\) distinct odd-offset neighbors. The complete equation list \(T_j=1\) telescopes under shift two, forcing \(4r\)-periodicity of any solution. Regularity forces \(2r\mid n\). If \(4r
mid n\), the shorter period makes every neighbor sum even, contradicting one. If \(4r\mid n\), every opposite-parity residue class occurs exactly once in each neighborhood. Selecting one residue class of each parity is both necessary and sufficient, yielding exactly \((2r)^2\) codes. The standalone verifier passed six literal subset enumerations, 45 independent recurrence enumerations, and 7,800 direct construction checks. None of the finite checks replaces the infinite proof.

Direct comparisons with relevant primary full-text sections of 2025/2026 Cayley and Cayley-sum papers distinguish the all-lift rigidity from base-case theorems and from limited subgroup/coprimality situations. value.rationale: Total perfect codes and efficient open domination are directly motivated by the two recent primary papers. The complete two-parameter classification of connected odd-step circulants includes all orders, including larger cyclic lifts that are not covered by the existing base-case classification. It gives exact existence, every code, and the stable number \((2r)^2\) across arbitrarily large lifts. The bounded universal period is a structural insight rather than an arbitrary parameter choice or isolated computation.
